after=[v for t,v in d.items() if t>='2018-06-15']
print("before n",len(before),"mean",sum(before)/len(before))
print("after n",len(after),"mean",sum(after)/len(after))

# hour-of-day means

    m=defaultdict(list)
    for t,v in vals:
        m[int(t[11:13])].append(v)
    return {h:round(sum(x)/len(x),2) for h,x in sorted(m.items())}
print("BEFORE by hour, mid-June window 06-01..06-14")

print(hod(bf))

content.text: The data show the F2_Z01 cooling setpoint dropped a flat ~1C across **all** hours (occupied 24.39→23.34, setback 26.7→25.7) starting around June 14, while every other core zone stayed unchanged. A uniform constant offset across the whole day profile (occupied *and* setback hours) is the signature of a controller offset / local override, not a schedule change (which would alter which hours or the time-varying profile).
